title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the setup of the previous one (34)-(39). There, Grothendieck takes P^1(C) with ramification indices nu_* = (nu_0, nu_1, nu_inf) at 0, 1, inf. This is a 'multiplicité topologique', in modern terms the orbifold P^1(nu_0, nu_1, nu_inf), viewed as a topos. He identifies its fundamental group with pi_{0,3}/<rho_i^{nu_i}>, where pi_{0,3} = pi_1(P^1 - {0,1,inf}) is free on two generators. The 'tau-version' adds complex conjugation and gives the non-orientable orbifold quotient: pi^tau_{0,3}/<rho_i^{nu_i}>. After profinite completion these become etale fundamental groups of the corresponding orbifold P^1 over Qbar, resp. over Qbar ∩ R.

The page first draws the consequence that Gal(Qbar/Q) acts by outer automorphisms on all these profinite quotients, and in particular on hat-pi_{0,3} itself. This is the Belyi/Esquisse Galois action.

It then singles out three cases, interpreting each group as a 'cartographic group' whose finite permutation representations classify maps.

(I) nu_0 = nu_1 = nu_inf = inf. The groups pi^tau_{0,3} and pi_{0,3} classify general triangulated maps (in modern terms hypermaps/dessins, via the barycentric triangulation), non-oriented resp. oriented.

(II) nu_1 = 2 (edges). The groups pi^tau_{0,3}/<rho_1^2> and pi_{0,3}/<rho_1^2> classify ordinary maps.

(III) nu_0 = inf, nu_1 = 2, nu_inf = 3. The groups pi^tau_{0,3}/<rho_1^2, rho_inf^3> and pi_{0,3}/<rho_1^2, rho_inf^3> classify ordinary maps (not general ones) whose faces have degree dividing 3, i.e. monogons or triangles. The oriented and non-oriented cases are distinguished in the text.

Via (35)/(36) he then states two isomorphisms (numbered (40) on the next page):
- pi^tau_{0,3}/<rho_1^2, rho_inf^3> ≅ pi_1(U_{0,3}, S_3 x {1,tau}; P_+) =: pi^{D_3,tau}_{0,3};
- pi_{0,3}/<rho_1^2, rho_inf^3> ≅ pi_1(U_{0,3}, S_3; P_+) =: pi^{D_3}_{0,3}.

Here pi_1(X, G; P) is the equivariant (orbifold) fundamental group of X with its G-action. The point is that U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,inf} modulo the anharmonic group S_3 (the six cross-ratio substitutions) is the orbifold P^1(2, 3, inf), i.e. the j-line. Its points of order 2 and 3 come from {-1, 1/2, 2} and {e^{±i pi/3}}. Adding complex conjugation gives the non-orientable quotient.

The bottom-left formula {rho_1, rho_inf | rho_1^2 = rho_inf^3 = 1} records that the oriented group is Z/2 * Z/3. A slanted marginal note says these isomorphisms hold in general for operator groups G acting on a space X, through pi_1(X, G; P), with some rigidification condition; the note is partly illegible.

On the next page the isomorphisms are written out explicitly. Replacing U_{0,3} by the Poincaré upper half-plane gives PSL(2,Z) ≅ pi^{D_3}_{0,3} and PGL(2,Z) ≅ pi^{D_3,tau}_{0,3}. So triangular maps are classified by subgroups of the modular group, and non-oriented ones by subgroups of the extended modular group.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The conditions are consistent: nu_inf = 3 forces faces of degree 1 or 3; S_3 acting on P^1 - {0,1,inf} has quotient orbifold of signature (2, 3, inf); and the free group of rank 2 modulo rho_1^2, rho_inf^3 is Z/2 * Z/3 ≅ PSL(2,Z).

Minor: the case list first said 'les deux suivants' (the two following), corrected to three cases. In case III the phrase 'cartes triangulées' was struck and refined into 'faces of order dividing 3', which correctly includes monogons.

ideas.what: Gal(Qbar/Q) acts by outer automorphisms on profinite completions of orbifold fundamental groups of P^1 minus 3 points with prescribed ramification, in particular on hat-pi_{0,3}
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the profinite free group F_2 hat (Belyi / dessins d'enfants)

ideas.what: Finite-index subgroups / finite sets with action of the triangle-type quotients of pi_{0,3} (and their tau-extensions) classify hypermaps, ordinary maps, and triangular maps, oriented or not
ideas.modern_name: Cartographic groups; map/hypermap theory via triangle groups
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme, §§2-3 (cartographic groups C_2, C_2^+)

ideas.what: pi_{0,3}/<rho_1^2, rho_inf^3> ≅ pi_1^orb(U_{0,3}/S_3) ≅ PSL(2,Z), and the tau-version ≅ PGL(2,Z), via the anharmonic group acting on P^1 - {0,1,inf}
ideas.modern_name: Modular group as the orbifold fundamental group of the j-line; extended modular group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein / Fricke); in map theory Jones–Singerman
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (triangulated maps and SL(2,Z)/±1)

ideas.what: Equivariant fundamental group pi_1(X, G; P) of a space with a group of operators, and its identification with an orbifold fundamental group of the quotient (marginal remark that such isomorphisms hold in general)
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold / equivariant fundamental group; fundamental group of a quotient stack [X/G]

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working-out of the cartographic-group and modular-group dictionary that Grothendieck published in the Esquisse and that the map-theory literature (Jones–Singerman) already had. The non-oriented versions and the topos/orbifold framing are also standard. Nothing here appears absent from the record.
transcription_corrections: Case I: 'pi_{0,3}^{±}' should read pi_{0,3} (the superscript tau is crossed out in the image), i.e. 'on obtient pi^tau_{0,3} et pi_{0,3}'.

Case III: the inserted text reads roughly 'i.e. dont toutes les faces sont des monogones ou des triangles' (i.e. of order dividing 3), with oriented and non-oriented cases distinguished. 'Biangles' is doubtful, since degree 2 does not divide 3.
Under the first underbrace: 'groupes cartographiques triangulés, non or. resp. orientés'.

The marginal note is largely illegible. It appears to say the isomorphisms are valid generally for groups of operators G on a space X via pi_1(X, G; P), with some rigidification hypothesis; the reading is uncertain.
